settings.topic: A rainy walk and a kind neighbour

paragraphs.text: After lunch, I went for a walk. The sky was gray, and soon rain began to fall. I had no umbrella, so I turned toward home. At the corner, my neighbor, Mr. Lee, stood beside his gate. He held out a spare umbrella. “Here, take this,” he said. “You can bring it back tomorrow.” I thanked him and opened it. The rain tapped softly above me as we walked down the street together. Mr. Lee told me he was going to the small shop, so I went with him. We talked about the garden and the wet leaves along the road. At the shop door, he smiled and said, “Keep the umbrella until the rain stops.” I promised to return it the next day. On the way home, I felt warm, even though my coat was damp. A kind neighbor had made a rainy afternoon feel bright.

After lunch, I went for a walk. The sky was gray, and soon rain began to fall. I had no coat, so I turned toward home. At the corner, my neighbour, Sam, stood by his gate. He held out a large coat. “Here, take this,” he said. “You can bring it back tomorrow.” I thanked him and put it on. The rain fell on the street as we walked together. Sam said he was going to the shop, so I went with him. We talked about the garden and the leaves on the ground. At the shop door, he smiled. “Keep the coat until the rain stops,” he said. I promised to return it the next day. On the way home, I felt warm, even though my shoes were wet. “That was kind of you,” I said. Sam laughed. “It was no trouble. A walk is better with a friend.” I went home glad that I had met my kind neighbour.
